text: From the acceleration equation ä/a = −(4πG/3)(ρ + 3p/c²) + Λc²/3, a single fluid with equation of state p = wρc² can drive accelerated expansion (ä > 0) only if:
explanation: Acceleration requires the source ρ + 3p/c² < 0, i.e. p < −ρc²/3, i.e. w < −1/3. Matter (w = 0) and radiation (w = 1/3) both give ρ + 3p/c² > 0 and therefore decelerate the expansion; radiation decelerates even harder because its effective source is 2ρ. A cosmological constant (w = −1) satisfies w < −1/3, which is why Λ can drive acceleration.
